newsitem.title: ABU DHABI: AIOC to pump first Caspian oil by year end.
newsitem.headline: AIOC to pump first Caspian oil by year end.

text.p: Azerbaijan International Operating Company (AIOC) will start producing oil from its Caspian Sea fields by the end of this year, AIOC president Terence Adams said on Tuesday
Output would reach 120,000 barrels per day (bpd) in two years time from an initial 10,000 bpd from the Chirag-1 platform, he told reporters on the sidelines of an energy conference in Abu Dhabi.

"Early oil will go north...it's a sophisticated oil swap," Adams said, in reference to the initial agreement with Russian pipeline operator Transneft that allows AIOC oil into the Russian pipeline network in exchange for crude at the Russian Black Sea port of Novorossisk, a gateway to European markets.
Already 50,000 tonnes of Azeri oil was in storage at the border between Azerbaijan and Russia and it was planned that this oil would enter the Russian pipeline system in April.
Offshore lines from the Chirag-1 platform would be brought onshore at the end of August and a second plaform would go into operation in 1999, Adams said.

AIOC, whose production-sharing agreement to develop the Azeri, Chirag and deep-water Gunashli fields was ratified in 1994, is a major consortium of foreign firms led by British Petroleum Plc and Norway's Statoil, and including Amoco Corp and Exxon.
The fields contain four billion barrels of crude reserves, allowing output to reach 700,000 bpd in the first half of the next decade, Adams said in a paper delivered to the conference.
